catalog.title: Measure what probes and policies cost
catalog.mac: Research methods: Author request, review inputs, then open execution and evidence. Both CLIs use science interview/draft/publish and the same managed engine.
outputs: One cost-report.json in a new run: every measured response, summary statistics with dispersion, the effective configuration, and hardware and library identities, for up to six configurations in a fixed workload and in ordinary generation.
catalog.restriction: Measures one model on the hardware it runs on, and sets no target. It runs on the Python engine with a prepared model; no model is downloaded. A value the backend cannot report is recorded as not available, not as zero. The result does not show that a probe predicts well or that a policy helps.

actions.authorityReason: Inspect staged scientific inputs and execution resources without execution or authorship.
Execute a reviewed scientific operation and retain its scientific output type.

access.restriction: Calls the existing route with its existing service role and scientific gates. Request path parameters, query and body remain explicit; this adapter does not change execution topology or retry mutations.

interview.title: Measure what probes and policies cost
interview.purpose: Measure the time, memory, and evidence size that probe readings and intervention policies add to generation on one model. Each configuration is repeated in a shuffled order after a warm-up, and the report gives the spread, not a single timing.

fields.label: Model to measure
fields.help: Choose a model that is already prepared where this will run. Nothing is downloaded.

fields.label: Exact model version
fields.help: The 40-character commit of that model. The probes and policies must have been made for this same version.

fields.label: Reviewed prompt file
fields.help: A JSONL file with one object per line, each with an id and a prompt. Use a small sample of the prompts the study will use: at most 64, and a handful is usually enough.

fields.label: Probes to read
fields.help: One saved probe file per line, such as runs/<run>/trained.probe.json. Leave blank to skip the two probe-reading configurations.

fields.label: A policy that never acts
fields.help: A published intervention.policy.json whose strength is always zero. It shows what an attached policy costs when it changes nothing. Leave blank to skip.

fields.label: A policy that always acts
fields.help: A published policy with one fixed, nonzero strength. Leave blank to skip.

fields.label: A policy that acts on a probe score
fields.help: A published policy with a threshold or adaptive rule. Leave blank to skip.

fields.label: Also measure keeping activations
fields.help: true adds a sixth configuration that keeps the activations behind each probe reading, up to the byte budget below. It needs at least one probe.

fields.label: Token budget per response
fields.help: Tokens to generate. The fixed workload generates exactly this many in every configuration; ordinary generation may stop sooner.

fields.label: Measured repeats
fields.help: How many times each configuration is measured on each prompt. More repeats give a steadier spread and take longer.

fields.label: Warm-up rounds
fields.help: Complete rounds run first and kept out of the summary, because the first use of a model is slower. Their rows stay in the report.

fields.label: Seed for the order
fields.help: Each round runs the configurations in a different shuffled order chosen from this seed. The order used is written into the report.

fields.label: Prompt rendering
fields.help: chatTemplate or raw. It must match the rendering the probes and policies were made for.

fields.label: Sampling temperature
fields.help: 0 takes the most likely token each step. Above 0, every configuration uses the same sampling seed for a given prompt and round.

fields.label: Sampling seed
fields.help: Used only when the temperature is above 0.

fields.label: When probes are read
fields.help: prefill reads the prompt, decode reads each generated token, and both is the usual study setting.

fields.label: Read before or after steering
fields.help: preAction or postAction, as in a study's measurement settings.

fields.label: Reading budget per response
fields.help: The most probe scores kept for one response, as in a study's measurement settings.

fields.label: Activation byte budget
fields.help: The most activation bytes kept for one response in the sixth configuration. Keep it small.

fields.label: Device
fields.help: auto chooses a CUDA GPU, then an Apple GPU, then the CPU. Name cuda, mps, or cpu to choose.

fields.label: Model precision
fields.help: auto uses the device's usual precision. Use the precision the study will run in, because the probes were fitted for one.

interview.claimBoundary: Costs are measured for this model, hardware, prompts, and token budget. No target is set, and nothing here shows that a probe predicts well or that a policy helps.
questions: Which small set of prompts stands for the study's workload?
Which probes and policies will the study really use?
